ai.description: *Pseudophilautus kani* is a small shrub frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct dark interorbital markings. It features a pointed snout and granular skin on its flanks and belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Pseudophilautus kani* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark brown or blackish longitudinal band running from the snout through the eye to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Pseudophilautus kani* inhabits the mid-to-high elevation tropical montane cloud forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at altitudes above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kani Bushfrog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden in dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Pseudophilautus kani* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs in tree holes, primarily during the monsoon.
ai.distributionRemarks: Pseudophilautus kani is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Kerala, specifically inhabiting mid-elevation rainforests.
ai.callDescription: The Kani Bushfrog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation within its humid, forested mountain habitat.
